analysis_goal: Extract reusable academic research tool video structure for product-safe TikTok workflows.
account_positioning: A student/research productivity account using late-night academic pain, handheld laptop proof, and fast result promises to sell research workflow shortcuts.
main_content_logic: Sleepless-night pain hook -> tool promise -> topic input -> curated paper/result proof -> completed RRL/review output -> sleepy relief ending.

visible_sequence: saying goodbye to my sleepless night because i can now finish my rrl in 7 mins 🥹🥹🥹
skolar.ai provides me with research papers that are curated and relevant 🧑‍💻✨
just type your topic and let skolar work its magic 🪄✨
RRL done in 2-3 minutes, goodnight world 🥱💤
caption_logic.punctuation_pattern: All lowercase, emotional student phrasing, very short sentences, repeated cute emojis, no formal CTA. Strong time/quantity promises drive urgency.
caption_logic.first_frame_text_density: Medium-high: 4-5 large lines centered over a paper/laptop screen. The text is readable and emotional, less dense than the soft.student.era template.
caption_logic.command_grammar: “just type your topic” + “let [tool] work its magic” + numeric result proof + sleepy relief ending.
caption_logic.reuse_rule: Reuse the sleepless-night pain, simple input, result proof, and relief ending. Do not reuse unsupported exact time guarantees like “finish RRL in 7 mins” unless product evidence supports it.

viral_patterns.hook_type: late-night pain relief + fast academic workflow promise
hook_examples: saying goodbye to my sleepless night because i can now finish my rrl in 7 mins
just type your topic and let [tool] work its magic
RRL done in 2-3 minutes, goodnight world
viral_patterns.opening_0_3s: Show a laptop/paper/research document in dim late-night setting while the caption names a painful student outcome: sleepless night, RRL, thesis, research deadline.
middle_structure: Reveal the research tool website/interface, not necessarily a full landing page.
Show the simplest action: typing a topic or starting a search.
Show the tool producing or listing relevant papers/results.
Use a number or visible result page as proof, e.g. paper count, sources tab, outline, references.
viral_patterns.ending_cta: No explicit button CTA. The conversion comes from emotional relief: “done”, “goodnight”, “finally”, plus post hashtags for college/research/thesis search.

visual_style.camera: Handheld laptop filming, dark room / late-night desk, visible keyboard and screen tilt. No polished screen recording.
visual_style.pace: 24 seconds, roughly 4-5 beats. Each caption holds long enough to read while the camera pans/tilts over the screen.
visual_style.subtitle_style: Large white bold text with black outline, centered or lower-center, TikTok-native lowercase wording, cute/sleepy emojis.
visual_style.music: Likely soft/trend audio; captions carry the message.
visual_style.composition: Mostly laptop screen with keyboard foreground, occasional paper/PDF view. Screen angle and handheld imperfection make it feel student-made.

why_it_works: The pain is instantly recognizable for thesis/RRL/literature review students: sleepless nights and deadline pressure.
It shows a simple action instead of explaining many features, so the tool feels easy.
It uses numeric proof, “58 research papers”, which makes the result concrete.
The ending emotion is relief, not sales: “goodnight world” makes the benefit feel personal.
The laptop-screen filming makes it feel like a peer sharing a hack, not a brand ad.
viral_patterns.reuse_risk: Medium-high. The structure is reusable, but exact time promises like 7 mins or RRL done in 2-3 minutes may overpromise. For Literfy/Citely/FigPad, rewrite as “start faster”, “find relevant papers”, “get a structured starting point”, or “prepare sources for review” rather than claiming a finished academic task is complete.

recommended_templates.best_for: Literfy first, then Citely source checking, less directly FigPad unless framed as slide/figure deadline relief.

timeline.content: Late-night laptop/paper shot + sleepless thesis/RRL pain caption.
Show product page or feature with a short value line: curated papers, verified sources, editable figure workflow.
Type topic / paste reference / upload figure / click search.
Show paper list, source verification result, outline, references tab, export, or editable output.
End with “finally a starting point”, “sources organized”, or “goodnight world” style relief without overclaiming.

publishing_copy_logic.pattern: Short factual feature note + cute emojis + college/RRL/studytok/research/thesis hashtag cluster.
publishing_copy_logic.safe_rewrite_pattern: Mention the specific product result shown, keep student relief tone, avoid saying the work is fully done or guaranteed accurate.

compliance_notes: Avoid exact completion-time claims unless verified in product data.
Do not tell students the product completes their RRL/thesis for submission.
Position Literfy as finding real papers, organizing sources, and creating a starting point for human-reviewed literature review work.
Keep the emotional “goodnight world” relief, but make the result academically responsible.
